key_findings.finding: One meaningful source rule is not directly requested: only characters trigger encounters. Existing encounter questions assume a character or concern card resolution after triggering; they do not test whether another unit may claim the encounter.
All 59 expected answers were checked. No material source contradiction in the existing answer keys was found. The proposed addition does not require changing any existing entry.
The current source-coverage-map.json contains 88 procedural passage entries, while coverage-ledger pass15 describes 86. This is a bookkeeping discrepancy, not an additional missing rule.

proposed_additions.wording: May a mech or worker resolve an encounter or remove its encounter token merely by entering that territory?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: No. Only characters trigger encounters. A mech or worker entering a territory does not resolve its encounter or remove the encounter token; it remains for a character.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p.5, TYPES OF UNITS: characters can have encounters; other units have different roles.
Rulebook PDF p.24, ENCOUNTERS: Only characters will trigger an encounter. Token removal occurs when resolving the character-triggered encounter.
Rulebook PDF p.31, ENCOUNTERS: Only characters may have encounters.
proposed_additions.novelty: A categorical unit-eligibility restriction with a consequential board-state outcome. Q15 asks timing after contested entry, the losing-character branch, benefit placement and isolated costs; Q36 asks stopping and timing when a character arrives via Factory Move; Q46 asks information presentation; Q54 asks choosing options after drawing. All can be answered correctly while incorrectly allowing a mech or worker to trigger an encounter. Q16 explicitly asks who takes a Factory card, but Factory eligibility does not elicit encounter eligibility. Q05 only asks movement/carriage, Q30 combat eligibility. The additional question introduces no changed quantities, new layout, unrelated combination or reference-only procedure.

limitations: This finding is a coverage judgment against the supplied authoritative booklet, not against FAQs, later editions, card databases or play variants.
PDF text was verified in full. The source-only images on pp19 and 29 were visually inspected; other pages were read via their verified text rather than every decorative image.

Question-wording elicitation is judged at the meaningful rule level. Generic optional-benefit, exposed-cost and already requested resolution rules were not exploded into every possible physical or numerical instance.
